s1-p01-018: We developed a low-cost first-stage bridge vibration screening system that observes bridge vibration together with environmental variables using a low-cost MEMS accelerometer and a temperature/humidity sensor, compensates for normal variation explained by temperature and humidity, and detects only the remaining change as anomaly candidates.
s1-p01-019: 2. Description of the project (proposed solution and its rationale)
s1-p01-020: Damage in aging bridges accumulates between inspections, yet small and medium bridges lack a low-cost means of continuous monitoring. This project collects vibration and temperature/humidity with an ADXL355Z accelerometer, a DHT22 temperature/humidity sensor and a Raspberry Pi, compensates the frequency features with a temperature/humidity regression learned on normal data, and then trains an Autoencoder unsupervised on those residuals alone; when the reconstruction error exceeds the threshold (the normal 99th percentile), it flags an anomaly candidate and shows the bands that departed. The design rests on two facts: natural frequencies change with temperature and humidity even without damage, and damage data are hard to obtain from real bridges.
s1-p01-022: Existing low-cost MEMS SHM studies do not address environmental compensation, fiber-optic (BOCDA) precision measurement requires dedicated infrastructure, and unsupervised studies on public data mostly stop at outputting an anomaly score. This project is distinguished by integrating measurement, environmental compensation, anomaly judgment and band-wise explanation into a single low-cost device.

Results  In the model-bridge experiment, adding 100 g on the left and right lowered the first peak frequency by 8.9%, confirming detection of mass change, and temperature/humidity compensation improved the F1 score about 4.9-fold, from 0.075 to 0.370, and the false-alarm rate in the humidity segment from 17.5% to 9.1%. On full-scale bridge data from Germany's openLAB, the false-alarm rate also decreased consistently after compensation.

Project topic  We developed a low-cost first-stage bridge vibration screening system that observes vibration and the environment together with a MEMS accelerometer and a temperature/humidity sensor, compensates for normal variation explained by temperature and humidity, detects only the remaining change as anomaly candidates, and also shows the bands that departed.
s2-p01-018: 2. Description of the project (proposed solution and its rationale)
s2-p01-019: Class 3 small and medium bridges, 64.5% of all bridges in Korea, lack a low-cost means of continuous monitoring to fill the gap between precision diagnoses. This project collects 500 Hz vibration and temperature/humidity with an ADXL355Z, a DHT22 and a Raspberry Pi 5 (about ₩190,000) under excitation from a solenoid auto-tapper, compensates eight log/ratio-normalized features with a temperature/humidity regression learned on normal data, trains an Autoencoder unsupervised on the residuals alone, flags an anomaly candidate when the reconstruction error exceeds the threshold, and shows the band contributions on a dashboard. The design rests on the facts that natural frequencies change with temperature and humidity even without damage and that damage data cannot be obtained from real bridges.
s2-p01-020: 3. Differences from existing work (solutions)  Existing low-cost MEMS studies do not address environmental compensation, KRISS's fiber-optic (BOCDA) precision measurement requires dedicated infrastructure, and unsupervised studies on public data mostly stop at outputting an anomaly score. This project is distinguished by integrating measurement, environmental compensation, anomaly judgment and band-wise explanation into a single low-cost device.
s2-p01-021: 4. Results  In the environment × mass × bolt experiment with 27 conditions (1,380 windows), the compensated model detected all 840 damage windows (recall 100%, F1 0.998), with 4/90 false alarms (4.4%). Over 5 repeated seeds, only the compensated model kept 100% for every seed (uncompensated 96.2–99.3%). The anomaly score grew with the severity of damage (5.8× → 22.6×), and bolt loosening (40–80 Hz) and mass change (amplitude/energy) were distinguished by their contributing features. The reduction in false alarms from compensation was confirmed in the humidity segment of the stage-1 experiment, 17.5% → 9.1%, and was reproduced in the same direction on full-scale openLAB data.
s3-p01-017: 1. Project topic  We developed a low-cost first-stage bridge screening system that records vibration and the environment together with a MEMS accelerometer and a temperature/humidity sensor, compensates for normal variation explained by temperature and humidity, alerts only on the remaining change as anomaly candidates, and also shows which vibration characteristic departed.
s3-p01-019: Class 3 small and medium bridges, 64.5% of all bridges in Korea, lack a low-cost means of continuous monitoring to fill the gap between precision inspections. This project collects vibration and temperature/humidity with an ADXL355Z, a DHT22 and a Raspberry Pi 5 (core parts about ₩190,000); it removes the part explained by a temperature/humidity regression from eight log/ratio-normalized vibration features, feeds the residuals to an Autoencoder trained only on normal data, flags an anomaly candidate when the reconstruction error exceeds the threshold, and reports the contribution of each feature. The design rests on the facts that natural frequencies change with temperature and humidity even without damage and that damage data cannot be obtained from bridges in service.
s3-p01-020: 3. Differences from existing work (solutions)  Existing low-cost MEMS studies do not address environmental compensation, fiber-optic (BOCDA) precision measurement requires dedicated infrastructure, and unsupervised studies on public data mostly stop at outputting an anomaly score. This project integrates measurement, environmental compensation, anomaly judgment and explanation of causes into a single low-cost device and validated it directly, from model experiments to real pedestrian overpasses.
s3-p01-021: 4. Results  In the 27-condition environment × mass × bolt experiment on the aluminum model, the compensated model detected all 840 damage windows (recall 100%) with false alarms on only 4 of 90 normal windows (4.4%), and its contributions distinguished bolt loosening from mass change. On public openLAB data, once the frequency channel was combined, temperature compensation reduced the autumn false-alarm rate from 26% to 0–3%. On two real overpasses, mode peaks were tracked within 1%; with a 200 kg load the frequency fell by 0.6% and returned after removal, and alarms sounded only in the loaded state, not in the unloaded state.
